Buscamos incorporar una persona Técnica de Soporte IT N0 para reforzar nuestro equipo de Soporte Técnico en Cornellà de Llobregat. Gestión y distribución de tickets (Dispatching) Recepción, clasificación y priorización de solicitudes e incidencias técnicas. Asignación de tickets a los técnicos o equipos correspondientes. Instalación de aplicaciones corporativas y actualizaciones de software. Verificación del correcto funcionamiento de los equipos y resolución de incidencias técnicas básicas. review_candidates.description: As a Medior Microsoft 365 Endpoint & Automation Engineer at HEMA, you will keep the workplaces of our colleagues running, from the checkout in the store to the laptop in the office, and make sure the same problems never need to be solved twice. Within the M365 Chapter, you will combine endpoint expertise in Intune and Windows with engineering skills in PowerShell, monitoring and automation to detect and remediate issues at scale. A hands-on role with visible impact in our stores. what you'll do For us, an endpoint is everything that runs Windows: the laptops in our offices, the checkout systems and other devices in our stores. As part of the M365 Chapter, you make sure these devices are configured, deployed, and, above all, healthy. It is not enough to know that the platform behind them is running. We want to understand the health of individual endpoints through telemetry, detect deviations automatically, and resolve issues before they affect store operations. We are doing this at the scale of thousands of endpoints, so manual checks are not an option. You will also contribute to our new physical Digital Workspace in the stores, including configuration, rollout, and supportability. The Chapter is on its way from a mainly operational team to an engineering-driven platform team. We are building up first-line capability at the Service Desk, so that intake, triage and standard solutions no longer land with us. Complex technical issues that require platform expertise remain with the Chapter. You investigate these issues, but importantly use what you learn to improve monitoring, automation, and the platform itself. Our ambition is a split of roughly 60% engineering and a maximum of 40% operations. That is a journey: today operations still take a large share of our time, and you will help us bring it down by treating recurring incidents as engineering problems: identifying the root cause, improving telemetry and implementing structural or automated solutions. You analyse root causes independently, build remediations and monitoring, and deliver your scripts and solutions through Git, pull requests and CI/CD. You take technical ownership of one or more endpoint services or capabilities, including their configuration, automation, monitoring, documentation and operational health. You contribute improvements to our engineering practices and support junior colleagues in their daily engineering work. You work from a DevOps mindset: you build it, you run it. We are not looking for a second-line support engineer who gets swallowed up by reactive tickets. We are looking for a hands-on Microsoft 365 Endpoint & Automation Engineer who uses troubleshooting as the starting point for engineering: turning recurring problems into monitoring, automation and structural improvements. what we offer At HEMA, you will learn and grow in an environment where people genuinely work together. You will receive guidance, valuable feedback, and plenty of opportunities to develop yourself. In addition, you will receive: 💸 A competitive salary based on your knowledge and experience. 🌴 30 vacation days (based on a 40-hour working week) and 8% holiday allowance. 🎯 A variable bonus of up to 14% of your annual salary, depending on collective performance. 💸 A monthly net expense allowance. 🎄 A fixed year-end bonus of 4% of your annual salary. 🛍️ 15% employee discount on all your HEMA favourites. 🧓 An excellent pension scheme. 🚗 Travel allowance of €0.23 per kilometre (from 10 km one-way travel up to a maximum of 30 km). 🎡 Access to our Benefits at Work platform, offering discounts on leading brands, experiences and activities. what you bring You are a hands-on engineer with a strong troubleshooting mindset who enjoys building and improving solutions in a team that takes ownership. You work independently on well-defined solutions, communicate comfortably with stakeholders such as the Service Desk and store operations, and understand the importance of delivering secure, maintainable and well-documented work. You use automation and modern engineering practices to solve endpoint problems structurally, and you are motivated to deepen your skills in Microsoft Graph, testing, and CI/CD. In addition, you bring: Bachelor's level of thinking and working, gained through education or relevant professional experience. At least 3 years of relevant experience in Windows endpoint management, workplace engineering or Microsoft cloud environments. Strong troubleshooting skills in Windows endpoint environments, including complex second and third-line issues. You understand endpoint security principles and consider security, least privilege and manageability when designing or changing endpoint configurations. Practical experience with Microsoft Intune and modern Windows endpoint management; experience with Configuration Manager (SCCM) is a plus. Experience writing and maintaining PowerShell for endpoint management, troubleshooting or automation. Experience working with Git, pull requests and CI/CD using Azure DevOps, GitHub or a comparable engineering platform. Practical experience with monitoring and automation, and experience delivering technical changes through Git-based workflows. Experience using logs, telemetry or endpoint analytics to investigate health and behavior across a larger device estate. Practical experience with Intune and Windows endpoint management, including configuration, application packaging and deployment, compliance and troubleshooting. Experience with Microsoft Graph, automated testing and CI/CD, or a demonstrable ability to grow into these technologies. A proactive mindset, strong collaboration skills, and a focus on delivering tangible results. HEMA At HEMA, more than 17,000 colleagues work together to make everyday life better and more beautiful. We create products that are practical, better designed, and built to last longer. Through our colourful stores, online channels, and strong partnerships, we continue to grow and evolve. We are proud of how far we have come, but we are far from finished. HEMA is truly HEMA again and ready for the next step. Our ambition is clear: to become a market leader in a challenging retail environment. We do this together as one team, by playing to win. That means being curious, seizing opportunities, collaborating with energy, and always striving for the best result. Will you join us?

Your mission will be to ensure that new sites and existing infrastructure have the routing, connectivity, hardware, and network resources required for reliable service delivery and future growth. Manage infrastructure readiness: Coordinate requirements involving rack space, power, security, cabling, cross-connects, hardware delivery, carrier access, and installation readiness. Align IP and Layer 1 delivery: Work with network and transport teams to establish clear responsibilities, service demarcation points, handoffs, and integrated delivery milestones. Plan IP connectivity: Coordinate the delivery of IP transit, peering, private interconnects, and backbone connectivity in alignment with global network architecture and business requirements. Support provider qualification: Coordinate technical due diligence with Network Architecture, Engineering, and Procurement, gathering ISP information, tracking qualification assessments, and documenting provider selection decisions. Coordinate routing resources and security: Oversee the lifecycle and accurate documentation of IPv4 and IPv6 allocations, ASN usage, AS-SETs, route objects, and Route Origin Authorizations (ROAs). Track routing security readiness: Coordinate RPKI and Internet Routing Registry (IRR) requirements during provider onboarding, routing changes, and new-site launches, working with technical owners to resolve issues. Coordinate backbone hardware and supply: Maintain forward-looking hardware demand forecasts and manage delivery coordination for routers, line cards, optics, spare components, software entitlements, and related infrastructure. Support hardware procurement: Work with IP Engineering, Network Supply, and Procurement to validate bills of materials, track purchase requests, monitor supplier commitments, and manage lead times and regional logistics. Manage project delivery: Build and maintain integrated project plans covering milestones, dependencies, owners, acceptance criteria, risks, and operational handover requirements. Drive cross-functional execution: Coordinate activities across IP Architecture, IP Engineering, Layer 1 Planning, Data Center Operations, Construction, Security, Procurement, and external service providers. Oversee launch coordination: Track testing, service activation, routing turn-up, documentation, and operational handover to ensure infrastructure is ready for production. Coordinate security initiatives: Support IP security and DDoS-related projects by managing scope, stakeholders, dependencies, milestones, risks, and delivery handovers while Security Architects retain technical ownership. Improve operational processes: Support incident follow-ups, provider escalations, project reviews, and continuous improvements in planning, connectivity resilience, provider diversity, and operational readiness. Strong understanding of IP backbone infrastructure, Internet connectivity, and network architecture, including IP transit, peering, private interconnects, and routing. Experience coordinating data center or Point of Presence (PoP) deployments, including connectivity readiness, hardware delivery, site dependencies, and service activation. Familiarity with Layer 1 and Layer 2 infrastructure concepts, including fiber connectivity, DWDM transport, cross-connects, optical handoffs, and network demarcation points. Understanding of Internet routing resources and security mechanisms, including IPv4, IPv6, ASN management, BGP-related resources, RPKI, IRR, AS-SETs, route objects, and ROAs. Experience coordinating network hardware procurement and supply processes, including routers, line cards, optics, bills of materials, supplier lead times, and logistics. Ability to build and maintain integrated project plans, define milestones, track dependencies, manage risks, and coordinate multiple technical workstreams. Experience working with network engineering, architecture, procurement, data center operations, security, and external infrastructure providers. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to facilitate technical discussions and drive decisions across distributed teams. Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail, particularly when managing complex dependencies, documentation, and delivery schedules. Proactive problem-solving abilities, with the confidence to identify risks, resolve blockers, and escalate critical issues when necessary. Ability to operate effectively in a fast-growing environment where project scope, priorities, and responsibilities may evolve with business needs. Professional proficiency in English and the ability to collaborate within an international technical organisation. Flexibility and ownership: Work with autonomy and take meaningful responsibility for high-impact infrastructure initiatives.
